thread:
alice: FYI customer ACME just escalated — streaming responses (SSE) p95/p99 shot up ~2x since ~2024-11-02 18:04 UTC. They see big TTFB on first chunk, but total non-streamed requests look OK.

alice: Repro steps I shared in ticket: single request to /v1/chat/stream with model=redwood-2, long-ish prompt (~1k tokens). Observed first-chunk delay ~600-800ms (baseline ~120ms). Attached traces + request ids.

sam: Do we have request_ids + a quick curl to repro locally? Also which infra region/customer routed region?

alice: Repro curl:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2","input":"<long prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/stream
```
Sample request ids: req_20241102_5401, req_20241102_5402. Region: us-west-2.

mira: Quick data point: runtime traces show KV cache warm misses for both requests, but the decoder token generation time looks normal. The delay is before first token emit — likely chunk flush scheduling or proxy coalescing.

jordan: Edge proxy metrics (us-west-2) show a spike in http2 stream buffer wait at ~18:03 corresponding to those req ids. Possible burst in connection pool -> coalescing behavior.

deploy-bot: deploy:runtime v2.17.3 -> v2.18.0 started at 2024-11-02T17:58:12Z by sam (sha:abc123).

sam: That deploy window matches. v2.18 included a change to streaming flush heuristics (batching window increased to 50ms). Might explain first-chunk TTFB regressions.

alice: Customer wants ETA and workaround. They're sensitive to p99 for interactive UX. We suggested non-streaming fallback for now, but need internal plan.

mira: Short-term mitigation ideas:
- force-first-chunk-flush: runtime option to emit first chunk immediately (zero window)
- reduce streaming batching window from 50ms->10ms for affected region/tier
- route affected customers to non-stream (sync) endpoints until fix

sam: I can cut a canary rollback to v2.17.3 in us-west-2 and observe p99. Prefer to test in staging first.

jordan: Ops note: if we adjust proxy coalescing, we might incur more small writes -> CPU/egress cost bump. Need sign-off.

alice: Customer ok with temporary non-stream fallback for their org if we can provide rollback ETA. They asked for probing steps to reproduce on their side — I gave the curl above.

sam: Plan of action (POA):
1) sam -> run staging repro + perf test against v2.18 and v2.17 (ETA 2h)
2) mira -> examine traces for KV/cache/perf counters and confirm flush queue delta (ETA 3h)
3) jordan -> measure proxy coalesce metrics and sanity-check pool saturation (ETA 1h)
4) if staging confirms regression, canary rollback in us-west-2 (ops) and notify customer (ETA 4-6h)

mira: Also adding a shorter-term runtime flag: `--emit-first-chunk-immediately` (dev note) to test if that removes TTFB. If yes we can enable for p99-sensitive tenants.

sam: I'll post a perf-run snippet here when done. For reproducibility, please include HTTP/2 vs SSE headers — some clients show different buffering.

alice: I'll keep the customer updated. Posting the telemetry link: <https://console.redwood-inference/internal/telemetry/req_20241102_5401> (internal).

jordan: Assigning ops oncall to monitor p95/p99 dashboards and alert if rollback needed: @ops-oncall.

adeploy-bot: noticed: config change to proxy coalescing threshold merged at 2024-11-02T17:30Z (pr#4779).

sam: Good catch — that may be two simultaneous changes (runtime flush + proxy coalesce). We'll isolate.

alice: Next updates in thread. Customer asked for a short workaround note to share: "We're temporarily routing streaming requests to the sync endpoint to avoid initial-chunk delays while we investigate; no changes to your prompt or API keys required."

mira: If anyone needs the raw traces, ping me and I’ll export flamegraphs.

sam: Action: I will run A/B: v2.18 with emit-first-chunk flag ON vs OFF in staging and measure TTFB p99. Will paste results here.

alice: Thanks — leaving note on ticket and tagging customer. :thumbsup:
